title: Writing pass after your send-back
body: You asked for the AI writing tics out of this and the other blueprints. A fresh register editor read the whole file against the developer-docs register and the house tells, and its 33 rewrites are applied. Every changed line was then fact-checked against its old wording, so no claim moved.

"own" is gone except one place, which quotes the engine error "Model it as the parent's own concept" verbatim. The register already bans the intensifier "own"; Survey backlog #1 adds a deterministic check so it is caught in all house writing.

title: A second entry at one address fails the build; backlog #31 tracks it
body: The edit page's advisory says "Publish this one and it replaces the other at that address" (`content-routes-entry-read.ts:412`). The 2026-06-23 advisory design meant last-write-wins.

The code disagrees. Once both entries are on `main` and neither is a draft, `createSiteResolver` throws on the duplicate permalink (`site-resolver.ts:86`), so the next build fails. The page states both behaviors as the code has them. cairn-cms backlog #31 reconciles the advisory with the resolver.

title: inFeeds has never been read; backlog #32 tracks it
body: `RoutingRule.inFeeds` came in with the first content model on 2026-05-28, and nothing in `src/lib` has read it since. Its doc comment says it decides feed and sitemap membership, which no code does.
The page says feed membership is the site's choice and leaves the flag out. cairn-cms backlog #32 removes the flag or wires it.

title: Renaming posts empties the scaffold's feed
body: The scaffold's feed reads `posts` by its id, so a site that renames the concept gets an empty feed with no error. The page gives this as a caveat telling the reader to update that code too. It isn't an engine fix.

title: The routing table is written as bullets
body: The plan wanted a table of the three routing values. The markdown blueprint format has no table form, so the rows are bullets under a lead-in that names them a table. The draft is expected to set them as a table.

title: Fact check fix: where updated shows up
was: `updated` is the sitemap's `lastmod` and the feed's modified date.
now: `updated` is the sitemap's `lastmod` and the entry page's SEO modified time. Only the JSON Feed carries a modified date, as `date_modified`, and only when the site's feed route passes it; the RSS feed carries none.
body: The fact `f:69j91g` said the same thing and is corrected with pointers to `public-routes.ts:174` and `feeds.ts:119`. The second fact check narrowed the feed half to the JSON Feed.

title: Fact check fix: the two dates agree to the prefix's granularity
was: An entry created in the admin starts with the two dates equal.
now: The filename prefix is the picked date cut to the concept's `datePrefix`, so the two agree to that granularity.
body: A concept with a year or month prefix doesn't carry the full date in its filename.

title: Fact check fix: the manifest row's optional fields
was: Its reference-field edges, tags, and included fragments, when it has them.
now: Adds media refs and the first-publish stamp.
body: The line had left out two of `ManifestEntry`'s optional fields.

title: The HTML pattern comparison rests on MDN
body: The line contrasting `pattern` with the HTML attribute cites `f:n26z3j`, an external fact from MDN. The fact-checker marked it unsupported only because no code in the repository can settle a browser behavior. MDN states that the attribute must match the whole value.

title: What the author corrected and dropped
body: The author corrected seven shared facts against the code. Among them, `content` takes a plain `ConceptConfig` (`defineConcept` is optional), a build verifies the manifest but doesn't regenerate it, and a rename rewrites only the links that `main`'s manifest records.
Under your D1 ruling, the charter's "no open-ended collection model" is dropped. The plan's "a rename or delete can warn" is also gone, because the code refuses instead of warning.
